title: [Decision] Ontology over external systems: virtual objects on ADR-0015 federation — two driver tiers (plugin code · declarative OpenAPI), pushdown/identity/catalog/cache rules, Studio and AI drafts (2026 ontology research + deep design)

## 维护者速读

- **一句话：** 把「行住在哪」从「我们的库 / 联邦数据库」扩到「任何有 API 的系统」，本体层（对象、关系、动作、权限、流程、Agent 工具）一个字不改；主流平台 2026 年的本体需求我们已有七成，缺的正是这一块加 Studio/AI 的「从外部系统生成本体草稿」。
- **要裁的：** §9 的六个决策点（两档都做还是只代码档；声明档映射键放哪；跨源联查保持非目标；缓存默认关；写回默认关；Studio 范围）。
- **工作量：** P0 spike S（#27130）；P1 代码档正式化约 3 个 M；P2 声明式 OpenAPI 数据源约 1 S + 2 M + 1 L；P3 增强按拉动。总计约 12–18 个 agent 天，分三次可独立交付。
- **推荐：** D1 两档都做但按序（代码档先，声明档等第二个客户）；D2 映射放 `object.external`；D3 保持非目标；D4 关；D5 关；D6 Studio 先只读。

## 1. Research: mainstream ontology needs in 2026, and the match

Sources are search summaries quoting the vendors' docs; `palantir.com` and `learn.microsoft.com` are not reachable from this session's network, so their pages were read through those summaries only.

| # | Need (who states it) | Mainstream shape | ObjectStack today | Gap |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| N1 | Ontology = semantic elements (object types, properties, links) + kinetic elements (actions, functions, dynamic security) — Palantir core concepts | objects / links / actions / functions | NORTH-STAR: objects, fields, relationships, actions, permissions, flows, agents, tools; formulas + hooks as functions; RLS + permission sets as dynamic security | none |
| N2 | Objects backed by data that is not moved: datasets and virtual tables (Palantir), zero-copy DLO → DMO (Salesforce Data 360), virtual tables over OData or a custom provider (Dataverse), remote tables fetched at query time (ServiceNow, 1,000-row default), entities bound to OneLake (Fabric IQ) | the object is a binding over a source | ADR-0015: federated DATABASES (schemaMode, `object.external`, three gates, catalog, service); backend / REST / CLI landed, Studio pending | **API-backed and computed sources** — this card |
| N3 | Writeback with governance: actions bundle edits + side effects; edits stored in a writeback dataset, not the source (Palantir); providers implement Create/Update/Delete (Dataverse); editing is opt-in (ServiceNow) | write gate + action semantics | hooks + actions on managed objects; ADR-0015 gate 3 (double opt-in `allowWrites` + `writable`) | an "edits overlay" for read-only sources (Palantir's writeback dataset) — not now |
| N4 | Agents consume the ontology: Ontology MCP exposes objects, predefined actions and queries with restrictions; typed OSDK; Data 360 MCP server (2026-05); Fabric IQ ontology as the agents' map; "active ontology via MCP" (Atlan) | MCP + typed SDK + action allow-lists | `packages/mcp` (`list_objects`, `describe_object`, `metadata_assistant`), client SDK packages, ADR-0025 plugin tools | action exposure and allow-lists per agent: partial (verify in a follow-up card) |
| N5 | A semantic / metrics layer for BI and text-to-SQL (dbt, Cube, AtScale; Snowflake semantic views GA 2026-03, Databricks metric views GA 2026-04) | metrics + dimensions defined once | `service-analytics` datasets and measures | fine for now; agents query via datasets |
| N6 | Ontology drafts generated from existing models: Fabric IQ's ontology agent proposes entities, relationships and rules from semantic models, schemas and documents (Gartner: may be incomplete / siloed) | generate, then curate | `IExternalDatasourceService.generateObjectDraft` / `importObject` from a remote DB | from an OpenAPI document — §4 P2; from documents — not now |
| N7 | Governance at the ontology boundary: security and compliance evaluated there, not at the model; RLS on virtual tables enforced in the source (Dataverse) | permissions on the object | object permission sets + RLS apply to federated objects "exactly as managed" (datasource guidance) | none |
| N8 | Rules on the ontology (Fabric IQ natural-language rules; ontology-constrained agents, arXiv) | validation rules | spec validation rules, refusals with prescriptions | natural-language rules — not our shape |
| N9 | Start small: one domain, 20–50 concepts, competency questions; FK links, join datasets for many-to-many | method | our strictness posture (AI-written ontology refused loudly) matches | none |

**Positioning read.** Palantir and Fabric IQ sit over lakehouses for analysis and decisions; Dataverse, ServiceNow and ObjectStack are OPERATIONAL ontologies — the ontology is the app (views, forms, flows, actions). Our differentiators hold: the ontology is written by AI and refused loudly when wrong, is diffable in the customer's repository, exportable, self-hostable. The one mainstream capability we lack in that operational class is the Dataverse "virtual table over an API with a custom provider" and its declarative OData sibling. That is exactly #27130's pull, generalized.

## 2. Goal and non-goals of this design

**Goal.** An external system's entities become ontology objects without moving data: rows are read through a driver (plugin code now; a declarative OpenAPI driver later), every consumer (views, reports, permissions, hooks, audit, MCP, SDK) sees a normal `Object` (ADR-0015 §3.1), writes go through the platform's gates. **Non-goals** (kept from ADR-0015 §2.2 and added): cross-datasource joins pushed down (reads across sources are id-based lookups and in-memory expands), distributed transactions, reverse DDL, replacing `DataSync` for bulk mirrors, an edits-overlay for read-only sources, natural-language rules, a lakehouse zero-copy engine.

## 3. Conceptual model (five layers, two driver tiers)

```
Ontology layer    object · field · relationship · action · permission · flow · agent/tool   (unchanged)
Binding layer     object.datasource → datasource.schemaMode ≠ managed → object.external { remoteName, writable, columnMap, [operations] }
Datasource layer  managed DB · federated DB (ADR-0015, driver-sql …) · API / computed (THIS: plugin driver, OpenAPI driver)
Driver layer      IDataDriver + supports (pushdown capabilities) + optional introspectSchema / registerExternalObject
Integration layer connectors (rest / openapi / mcp / imap / slack) — outbound actions from flows; unchanged, complementary
```

Tier A — **plugin driver (code)**: a server plugin publishes `driver.<name>` (`plugin.ts:1145–1158`); `find / findOne / count / update` as the system allows; the rest refuse by name. Any system, any computation. (#27130's route d.)
Tier B — **declarative OpenAPI driver**: one platform driver `openapi` that reads a datasource config `{ driver: 'openapi', config: { spec: ref, baseUrl, auth: credentialsRef, pageStyle, rateLimit } }` and an object binding `external.operations { list, get, create?, update?, delete? }` naming operationIds plus a `idField`; the driver maps `DriverQuery` to query parameters it can push down (declared per object: filterable / sortable / pageable fields) and does the rest in memory. Reuses `connector-openapi`'s document parsing (ADR-0023). No code for the standard REST case.

## 4. Protocol surface (spec) — kept minimal

- **Tier A: zero spec change.** Everything is already in the contract: plugin-contributed driver ids (`datasource.zod.ts:186`), `schemaMode` external, `external.allowWrites`, `external.validation.checkOnBoot` (`datasource.zod.ts:316`), `object.external` (`object.zod.ts:1296`), `IDataDriver.supports` for pushdown.
- **Tier B: two additive keys** (`Metadata-protocol: added`, minor): `object.external.operations` (optional; refused unless the object's datasource driver is `openapi`; each entry an operationId that must exist in the referenced document — checked at build) and `object.external.idField` (optional; default `id`). The `openapi` driver's `config` shape lives in the driver's own config contract (`driver/config-registry.zod.ts`), not in the datasource schema. `external_catalog` gains `source: 'openapi'` with the document hash as the drift signal.
- **Not added:** any URL on a view or page element (ruling C stands); a parallel `external_object` type (ADR-0015 §3.1); a cache key on the object (caching is datasource config).

## 5. Runtime rules (the three ADR-0015 gates, extended to API sources)

1. **DDL gate:** unchanged — forbidden on external objects.
2. **Boot validation:** DB sources introspect; API sources validate the OpenAPI document hash against the catalog snapshot and, when `checkOnBoot` is true, perform one `list` probe with `limit 1`; a plugin driver with no `introspectSchema` is validated by its own contract test (the guide requires one "shape pin" test per driver).
3. **Write gate:** `allowWrites` (datasource) AND `writable` (object) AND, for Tier B, the operation named (`update` without `operations.update` refuses at build). Writes are per record, one system at a time; `enforceTransactionOrigin` keeps cross-datasource writes where ADR-0057 put them.
4. **Pushdown and fallback:** the driver's `supports` says what it pushes down (filters, sort, pagination, `in`, aggregate); the engine applies the remainder in memory through ONE shared helper (`@objectstack/objectql` exports `applyDriverQueryInMemory`), with a hard row cap per datasource (`config.maxRows`, default 1,000 — the ServiceNow figure) and a loud refusal above it: "narrow the filter or mirror via DataSync".
5. **Identity:** `idField` must be stable and unique in the source; `columnMap` maps names only. Relationships across sources are id-based lookups; expands batch through `find` with an `in` filter when `supports.inFilter`, else `findOne` per id under the row cap.
6. **Caching:** off by default; `config.cache: { ttlSeconds }` per datasource caches `find` results keyed by query for that TTL; writes invalidate. Never for `managed`.
7. **Errors:** driver / HTTP failures map to the platform refusal envelope (`EXTERNAL_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE`, `EXTERNAL_WRITE_REFUSED` with the source's message), never a silent empty list.
8. **Credentials:** only `external.credentialsRef`; the egress allow-list per datasource host is a deployment setting, not metadata.
9. **Permissions and audit:** object permission sets and RLS apply unchanged; every external write is audited with the datasource name.

## 6. Studio and AI

- Studio (ADR-0015's pending half): a Datasources page listing managed / federated / API sources with health and catalog drift; an external object's fields shown read-only with their source; for Tier B an "import object from OpenAPI" flow that calls `generateObjectDraft` on the document's schema components (N6) and lets the author pick operations.
- AI: the same `generateObjectDraft` is an MCP tool (`list_remote_tables` / `import_object` are already in the service contract); the guide gives AI authors the three-way rule — computed rows, data that must not land, or real-time ⇒ virtual object; slow-changing reference data ⇒ real object + `DataSync` flow.

## 7. Phases and workload

| Phase | Content | Lane · size | Depends on |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **P0** | #27130 spike: plugin driver + external object boots, reads with filters, formula over `current_user`, hook → `driver.update`, gantt drag | server · S | — |
| **P1 — Tier A formal** | `applyDriverQueryInMemory` helper + row cap; `supports` honoured by the engine for plugin drivers; refusal envelope mapping; driver "shape pin" test template; guide "a virtual object: rows from your server" with the five business examples; Studio read-only field marking | objectql M · docs S · ui S | P0 |
| **P2 — Tier B declarative** | spec: `external.operations` + `idField` + catalog `source: 'openapi'` (S); `driver-openapi` package: document parsing reused from `connector-openapi`, list / get / update / create / delete mapping, pushdown declaration, paging styles, auth via `credentialsRef` (L); Studio import-from-OpenAPI + datasource page (M); `generateObjectDraft` for OpenAPI schemas (S); example: showcase binds a public OpenAPI sample as an object (S) | spec S · server L · ui M · devx S | P1 |
| **P3 — enhancements by pull** | cache TTL; `aggregate` pushdown; DataSync mirror recipe; edits overlay (if a customer needs edits on a read-only source) | per card | P2 |

Totals: P0 ≈ 0.5 agent-day; P1 ≈ 3–4; P2 ≈ 8–10; P3 by pull. About 12–15 agent-days through P2; calendar 4–6 weeks at two lanes. Each phase ships on its own: P1 serves the #27130 class of customer; P2 serves the no-code ERP / HR / MES integrations.

## 8. Risks

- Silent wrong rows when a driver ignores filters → the in-memory helper is applied by the ENGINE on anything the driver's `supports` does not claim; a driver cannot opt out of correctness, only of performance.
- Unbounded reads → the row cap refuses loudly; the guide names `DataSync` for mirrors.
- Source shape drift → catalog hash + boot probe (Tier B); shape pin test (Tier A).
- Credential leakage into metadata → only `credentialsRef`; the build refuses inline secrets (existing rule).
- Two doors for writes → none: the view-level `api` stays retired; all writes are `driver.update` under the gates.
- Over-building Tier B before a second customer → P2 is gated on pull (D1).

## 9. Decision points for the maintainer (defaults bold)

- **D1** Tiers: **both, in order — Tier A now (P0–P1), Tier B when a second customer asks for a no-code REST source** / Tier A only / both now.
- **D2** Tier B mapping keys live on **`object.external.operations` + `idField`** / on the datasource config.
- **D3** Cross-datasource joins pushed down: **stay a non-goal** (ADR-0015 §2.2); id-based lookups and in-memory expands only.
- **D4** Caching: **off by default**, opt-in TTL per datasource.
- **D5** Writes: **off by default** (ADR-0015 double opt-in stands), per-operation for Tier B.
- **D6** Studio: **read-only field marking in P1; datasource page + OpenAPI import in P2** / all in P1.

os-decision-facets
- ① 项目长远合理性：本体层零改动、外部性仍是绑定的属性（ADR-0015 §3.1），两档 driver 补齐 Dataverse 式「虚拟表 + 自定义/OData 提供者」；不新增 `api` 视图源、不新增并行对象类型。
- ② 实际业务拉动：#27130 是第一个实测生产者（代码档）；声明档等第二个客户（ERP/HR/MES 的无代码接入）再建。
- ③ 防 AI 犯错：行、写回、锁定、权限全部是平台判定的元数据；driver 不能选择性忽略筛选（引擎兜底）；超行上限、形状漂移、缺操作映射全部响亮拒收。
- ④ 创业阶段不扩散：代码档零协议；声明档只加两个可选键；缓存、写回默认关；跨源联查、编辑覆盖层、自然语言规则不做。
Prior rulings read: ADR-0015 §1–§6, ADR-0049, ADR-0057 §3.6, #23082 C (6134088274), #23016, #27130 (6467643796 / 6468011868) → 6 hits; thread: none.

Tier-A-only ⇒ the same without P2. Both-now ⇒ P2 children filed at once, spec first.
